findings.title: Stray `sed -i` backup file committed
findings.description: The diff adds `CoreServiceFactory.test.ts-E`, and I confirmed the file exists on disk. This is the backup file BSD/macOS `sed -i` leaves behind, probably from the bulk edit of `createContextPipeline(...)` call sites. It is a full copy of the test file as it was before the edit, so it still calls `createContextPipeline(FIXTURE_PROJECT_PATH)` with one argument. It does not match the vitest `*.test.ts` pattern, so it won't run. It is still dead code that will mislead anyone grepping for call sites. Delete it, and consider adding `*-E` to `.gitignore`. The grep for that pattern in `.gitignore` found nothing.

findings.title: `'implementation'` default literal duplicated again
findings.description: The new line `const instruction = project.instruction || 'implementation';` adds a fourth copy of the default. Copies already exist at lines 216, 244 and 289, and `FileProjectStore.ts:104` has another. The project rules say a value used in conditionals or lookups should be defined once and referenced everywhere, and that magic defaults belong at the config level. This new copy must stay in sync with `mapProjectToEnhancedContext`, because the resolver is handed this value and the mapper later applies its own default. If they drift, the resolver would judge eligibility on a different instruction than the one that selects the prompt. Extract a constant such as `DEFAULT_INSTRUCTION`. A fuller fix would resolve the instruction once and pass it down, but that goes beyond this slice.

findings.title: Resolver ordering and error propagation are consistent
findings.description:
I checked the resolver's step order against its doc comments.
- The guide check runs before any state write, so a guide without the profile leaves `adoption.state` unset. Test 12 and the "rejects a guide without the profile, before writing" test cover this.
- A write failure is wrapped as `AdoptionError` with `cause`, and the message names the escape hatch.
- `ContextIntegrator` rethrows `AdoptionError` before its blanket catch.
- The `isSelected` switch is exhaustive, with a `never` check in the default branch.

`createContextPipeline` now requires `adoptionStateWrites`, and every call site I found passes it. That covers `cf build` and `context_build` with `persist`, and `template_preview` and the existing tests with `read-only`. The parity test and the `contextTools` tests assert the persist/read-only split directly.

structured_findings.summary: Resolver ordering and error propagation are consistent
